# MM-P1-L2-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Scope
This manual covers preventive maintenance and routine inspection for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) installed in plant P1, line P1-L2. It is intended for use by maintenance technicians qualified on ring rolling equipment and by rotating equipment engineers responsible for reliability and safety. The document addresses mechanical fastening checks on the mandrel assembly, lubrication of the main roll bearing, visual inspections of drive components, and records to be retained. For procedure updates and engineering changes see ECN-2026-041. For operator handover and process-related steps, see SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated to read and apply the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque. Use calibration certificates traceable to plant metrology.
- Manufacturer-approved grease gun and grease cartridges compatible with the main roll bearing.
- Clean lint-free rags, inspection mirror, LED inspection light.
- Bearing puller and mounting sleeves as required for bearing removal and installation during corrective work.
- Lockout/tagout kit compliant with plant P1 standards, electrical and mechanical isolation devices.
- Maintenance tag forms and digital record entry device.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Coordinate with operations using SOP-P1-L2-01 for scheduled downtime and handover. Ensure process temperature is at safe handling condition in accordance with operational procedures prior to work.
- Apply lockout/tagout on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 following plant P1 LOTO protocol. Verify isolation mechanically and electrically before any disassembly.
- Review ECN-2026-041 to confirm that no recent engineering change affects the mandrel clamp or bearing assembly before proceeding.

Mandrel clamp bolt check and torque
- Inspect mandrel area for evidence of fretting, displacement, or shear on clamp hardware. Clean mating surfaces of debris and old lubricant to allow accurate assessment.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the tool to the specified value for the mandrel clamp bolts. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.
- With the wrench, apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt in a crisscross pattern to ensure even seating of the clamp. If any bolt fails to achieve the specified torque due to rounded heads, thread damage, or excessive run-down, do not reuse the bolt; replace per parts list and record the condition.
- After torquing, perform a torque verification pass to confirm retention of the specified torque after a short settling period. Document results in the maintenance record.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm cleanliness of grease fittings and purge contaminant before applying fresh lubricant. Use recommended grease as described in OEM documentation linked in the equipment file.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 145 hours. Maintain a lubrication log indicating start time, end time, and bearing condition at each lubrication event.
- Apply grease until factory-specified purge characteristics are observed from relief points, or until resistance indicates full charge. Avoid overfilling which can lead to thermal and seal issues.
- After lubrication, operate the machine under no-load conditions briefly to redistribute lubricant and then perform a visual check for leaks and seal integrity.

Bearing inspection and replacement
- If bearing condition monitoring or visual inspection indicates abnormal noise, temperature, or lubricant contamination, schedule bearing removal. Follow plant bearing handling practices and use clean staging area to prevent contamination.
- On reinstallation, ensure alignment of mounting surfaces and follow tightness practices described for mandrel clamp bolts where applicable. Retain all removed hardware for inspection and record replacement parts.

Routine visual inspection
- Inspect drive belts, couplings, and guards for wear or looseness. Confirm guard fastenings are secure and safety interlocks are functional.
- Check hydraulic and pneumatic connections for seepage. Any suspected line or fitting requiring tightening should be deferred to a qualified technician following isolation.
- Confirm the condition of electrical cable routing and strain reliefs. Do not perform electrical work without authorization and proper isolation.

Records and examples
- Maintain the maintenance log for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 in the plant document control system. Entries must include date, technician name, work performed, and readings or observations. Reference to related documents ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, and SOP-P1-L2-04 must be included when actions were performed because of or in support of those documents.
- Example entry: “Lubrication performed; main roll bearing reported normal clearance; grease applied per procedure; next lubrication scheduled after the interval recorded in system.” Record the exact interval as specified in this manual.
- Retain torque verification stickers or tags on the equipment with date and technician initials after each mandrel clamp bolt torque event. Archive torque wrench calibration certificate copies with the job file.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts retain the specified torque without evidence of thread stripping, rounding, or seating movement. No relative movement of the mandrel under static inspection after torque application.
- Main roll bearing shows no signs of grease contamination, pitting, or excessive play after lubrication and normal operation. Bearing condition is acceptable if no abnormal noise or heating is observed following the lubricating event and operational checks.
- All guards and safety interlocks remain functional, with no temporary bypasses in place. Any temporary condition must be corrected before return to operation.
- Records contain complete entries referencing ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, or SOP-P1-L2-04 when applicable, and include technician name, date, and observed condition.

Notes and rationale
- Tightness of mandrel clamp bolts directly affects ring concentricity and roll loading; therefore torque specification is enforced as a reliability control. Verification and documentation create an auditable trail.
- Regular lubrication at the specified interval controls contamination and wear in the main roll bearing. The interval balances lubricant life and production availability to maximize bearing life while minimizing unplanned downtime.
- Cross-reference to ECN-2026-041 ensures changes in component design are incorporated into the maintenance baseline. Operator procedures in SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 are cited to ensure safe coordination between maintenance and production.
